findings.what: Brief-639's binding Web slice item 6 ('Refusal -> focus: read details.axis/details.field off the DoorRefusal and focus the named control (AC7)') and TDD seam #16's required 'denied (viewer)' cell are not delivered, and the final report's AC7/AC9 rows claim they are. `refusalFieldForAxis`/`FA_REFUSAL_AXIS_FIELD` exist only in the new non-frozen runtime module (for the future claraWork_v4 tool) and are never imported anywhere under apps/web. `fa-row-actions.tsx` (CompleteParticularsDialog) and `fa-particulars-fields.tsx`, which the brief said to 'reuse ... unchanged', are indeed untouched by this branch, so the human door's dialog still only shows a generic banner via `DoorDialogRefusal` (components/common/dialog-refusal.tsx), never a per-field focus. The Playwright test literally titled 'an invalid answer names the dependent CONTROL, keeps the draft, and a valid one persists' (line 144) fills a fully VALID form (method=straight_line, start_date=2026-08-20, useful_life_months=60) and submits successfully -- it never submits an invalid answer, never asserts a control receives focus, and never asserts an axis-mapped message. No test in the file signs in as anyone other than 'owner@example.test', so the CLR04 'insufficient_role' denied path is never exercised in the browser, even though `fixed-asset-mock.mjs:438-462` implements the exact CLR37 axis:'drivers'/axis:'start_date' refusal bodies built specifically to drive this scenario -- they are dead code from the spec's point of view. A genuinely reachable invalid path also exists and goes untested: `particularsReadyToSubmit` never checks residual_cents against cost_cents, and MoneyInput applies no clamp, so a human can submit a residual exceeding cost and hit the server's CLR37 'residual' axis with no client-side gate and, per this finding, no field focus on the way back.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "refusalFieldForAxis|details.axis" apps/web --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts (excluding *.test.*) returns 0 hits; `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- apps/web/components/registers/` lists only fixed-asset-detail.tsx/.test.tsx, fixed-assets-register.tsx, fixed-assets-keyboard.test.tsx, work-asset-row.tsx/.test.tsx -- fa-row-actions.tsx and fa-particulars-fields.tsx are absent; reading fixed-asset-acquisition-walk.spec.ts:144-183 directly (no fill of an invalid value, no viewer sign-in, straight line to a successful save); fixed-asset-mock.mjs:438-462 shows the unused CLR37 refusal bodies. The final report's AC7 row ('done ... Axis -> CONTROL: refusalFieldForAxis + fa.axis cells') and AC9 row ('... invalid/saving with the draft kept, denied ...') cite this walk as evidence.
findings.fix: Either wire an axis/field -> focus behavior into fa-row-actions.tsx / FaDoorDialog (mirroring the runtime module's map) and add real Playwright cells that (a) sign in as a viewer and assert the CLR04 refusal renders with the asset intact, and (b) submit a residual-exceeding-cost (or another reachable) invalid value and assert the named control receives focus -- or, if this is intentionally deferred, say so explicitly as a named residual in 639-final.md and change the AC7/AC9 verdicts from 'done' to 'partial-with-named-residual' rather than citing the runtime-only helper and an unused mock branch as proof.

findings.where: apps/web/e2e/fixed-asset-acquisition-walk.spec.ts (Playwright run on the assigned rig, ports 3260/3261/3262)
findings.what: Two independent solo re-runs of this one spec file on this lane's own assigned ports both hung indefinitely immediately after test 4 of 7 completed ('an invalid answer ... persists', ok, ~15-18s) and never produced any further output (no pass, no fail, no timeout error) for 5+ minutes each, with the Node/Chromium processes still alive (not crashed). System load at the time was elevated (CPU 45%-85%, 80-108 concurrent node.exe processes), consistent with this being one of twelve lanes sharing the host rather than a deterministic defect in the ticket's own code -- the page and its route were independently confirmed correct via the jsdom unit tests (11/11 pass) and the route's presence in the production build manifest. I could not independently reproduce the report's specific '7 passed (26.3s)' figure on this host at review time.
findings.evidence: Background task boi8z99ty (first run) and b7apwusdu (retry) both stalled at the identical point (`ok 4 ... (14.6s)` / `ok 4 ... (18.4s)`, then silence); Get-Item on the output file showed an unchanged LastWriteTime/Length for 5+ minutes while the bound processes were still running; Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor LoadPercentage read 45% then 85%; Get-Process node count read 108 then 84.
findings.fix: Re-run `pnpm --filter @clara/web e2e -- fixed-asset-acquisition-walk` on ports 3260/3261/3262 when this host is not carrying other lanes' load, and confirm 7/7 pass with a timing close to the report's 26.3s; if the hang reproduces on a quiet host, treat it as a real flake in the test-to-test transition around test 4/5 rather than dismissing it as contention.
